cues.en: Mike: So I hope you enjoyed watching those videos about importing and working with the marriage and divorce rates data.
cues.zh: Mike：希望你喜歡剛才那些關於匯入與處理結婚率、離婚率資料的影片。

cues.en: I would like to now just take a few moments to give you some parting words of wisdom, which are not really only about this section, but really about the entire course
cues.zh: 現在想花點時間，給你一些臨別建議；這些不只適用於本節，其實也適用於整門課，

cues.en: and your entire career as a statistician or machine learning expert.
cues.zh: 以及你作為統計學家或機器學習專家的整個職涯。

cues.en: So, a couple morals of this story.
cues.zh: 這個故事有幾個啟示。

cues.en: Notice that what we did here and what I've also spoken about throughout the course is we started from basics, data importing.
cues.zh: 注意，這裡的做法，也是我整門課一直提到的，就是從基本功開始，先匯入資料。

cues.en: We did visualization, we cleaned the data, we visualized the data more, we did descriptive statistics, we did some inferential statistics and visualization.
cues.zh: 接著視覺化、清理資料、再做視覺化、描述統計，以及一些推論統計與視覺化。

cues.en: Notice, how much visualization is taking place in our progression through the journey of working with data.
cues.zh: 注意，在處理資料的整個歷程中，進行了多少視覺化。

cues.en: In fact, most of what we've done is processing and visualizing and trying to understand the data and getting P values and T values and so on.
cues.zh: 事實上，大多數工作都是處理、視覺化與試著理解資料，而取得 P 值、t 值等等，

cues.en: That was actually just a relatively small part, and that leads to my next moral of this story, which is when people are just coming into statistics
cues.zh: 其實只占相對小的一部分；這就帶到下一個啟示：剛接觸統計的人，

cues.en: or they don't really know much about statistics and machine learning, they think that statistics is all about this, it's all about running ANOVAs and regressions
cues.zh: 或不太了解統計與機器學習的人，會以為統計全都是這些，也就是跑 ANOVA、迴歸

cues.en: and correlations, and then you'd make a bar plot of the results.
cues.zh: 與相關，接著把結果畫成長條圖。

cues.en: But now you have gone through this entire course, you are not a novice, you are now on your way to being an expert and you know that all of this stuff
cues.zh: 但現在你已經學完整門課，不再是新手，正走向專家之路；你知道，所有這些事情

cues.en: is way more important than this stuff.
cues.zh: 遠比這些事情重要。

cues.en: Not to say that inferential statistics is unimportant, obviously this is very important, but the process of working with data
cues.zh: 這不是說推論統計不重要，顯然它非常重要，但處理資料的過程，

cues.en: is a lot of visualizing, cleaning, processing, more visualizing, and descriptive statistics to understand the data.
cues.zh: 包含大量視覺化、清理、處理、再視覺化，以及用描述統計來理解資料。

cues.en: And only at the very end do you actually start doing inferential statistics.
cues.zh: 只有到最後，才真正開始做推論統計。

cues.en: By the way, I'm sure there's a meme somewhere.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，我相信一定有這樣的迷因。

cues.en: someone more clever than me and younger than me can come up with a meme about how novices think that this is important, but the experts know that this is important.
cues.zh: 比我聰明、比我年輕的人，可以做一張迷因，說新手以為這個重要，但專家知道這個才重要。

cues.en: Maybe one day I'll see a meme about this on some Reddit subpage or something.
cues.zh: 也許哪天會在 Reddit 的某個子版看到。

cues.en: Anyway, a couple more morals of this story.
cues.zh: 總之，還有幾個啟示。

cues.en: It's one of my favorite expressions in data analysis.
cues.zh: 這是我在資料分析中最喜歡的話之一。

cues.en: When in doubt plot it out.
cues.zh: 有疑問，就畫圖。

cues.en: Visualize often and in multiple ways.
cues.zh: 經常視覺化，而且要用多種方式。

cues.en: Look for missing data or unusual data and descriptive statistics and visualization will help you find missing data or unusual or non-representative data.
cues.zh: 尋找遺失資料或不尋常的資料；描述統計與視覺化，會幫你找出遺失、不尋常或不具代表性的資料。

cues.en: You should do lots and lots of sanity checks.
cues.zh: 應該做很多、很多合理性檢查。

cues.en: Sanity checks are basically just ways of looking at the data to make sure that the data are what you think they are, and there isn't something suspicious
cues.zh: 合理性檢查基本上就是查看資料，確保資料確實如你所想，沒有可疑的地方，

cues.en: or something going wrong with the data.
cues.zh: 也沒有哪裡出了問題。

cues.en: So how do you do sanity checks?
cues.zh: 那要怎麼做合理性檢查？

cues.en: Well, you can check the data sizes, matrix sizes, you can write out vectorized computations using for loops to make sure you get exactly the same results,
cues.zh: 可以檢查資料大小、矩陣大小，也可以用 for 迴圈重寫向量化運算，確認得到完全相同的結果，

cues.en: this is a way of checking your code.
cues.zh: 這是檢查程式的一種方式。

cues.en: You can compare descriptive statistics before and after cleaning or processing the data.
cues.zh: 可以比較清理或處理資料前後的描述統計。

cues.en: You can check that the results from different data selections really are different if you expect them to be different.
cues.zh: 如果預期選取不同資料會得到不同結果，可以檢查它們是否真的不同。

cues.en: You can run correlations and check for correlations of exactly one, which means that you have exactly the same variable, that might indicate that there's an error somewhere.
cues.zh: 可以計算相關，檢查是否有恰好等於 1 的相關，那表示變數完全一樣，可能暗示某處有錯。

cues.en: Basically, just spending a lot of time investigating and trying to understand your data.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是花很多時間調查，試著理解資料。

cues.en: So you should always be critical with data, always start with the assumption that something is wrong, and then be willing to be proven otherwise.
cues.zh: 因此，對資料應該永遠保持批判態度，先假設有地方出錯，再願意接受證據推翻這個想法。

cues.en: This is basically like being a scientist.
cues.zh: 這基本上就像當科學家。

cues.en: The appropriate way to be a scientist is to approach the world thinking that everything is wrong, thinking that your hypotheses are wrong,
cues.zh: 當科學家的適當方式，是抱著一切都可能有錯的想法面對世界，認為自己的假設有錯，

cues.en: you think that your theories are wrong, you think that your models are wrong, and you collect data with the goal of disproving yourself, that's how you be a good scientist, you try to disprove your own beliefs.
cues.zh: 理論有錯、模型有錯，蒐集資料是為了反駁自己；好的科學家會試著推翻自己的信念。

cues.en: Now, of course, you don't want to take that to an extreme.
cues.zh: 當然，不要走到極端。

cues.en: You have to be willing to accept that sometimes things are right and everything is fine, but it's healthy to start with the assumption that something is wrong
cues.zh: 也要願意接受，有時事情是對的，一切都沒問題；但先假設某處有錯，是健康的態度，

cues.en: and you need to inspect your data to make sure that things are okay.
cues.zh: 而你需要檢查資料，確認一切正常。

cues.en: On the other hand, you also need to be open-minded.
cues.zh: 另一方面，也需要保持開放的心態。

cues.en: So start with hypotheses, start with some preconceived notions of what you expect, but don't assume that your hypotheses are always correct.
cues.zh: 可以先有假設，先有一些預期的想法，但不要認定假設永遠正確。

cues.en: So listen to the data and be willing to be proven wrong.
cues.zh: 傾聽資料，願意接受自己被證明是錯的。

cues.en: Let the data prove that your hypothesis is wrong, if that's what the data are really telling you.
cues.zh: 如果資料確實如此，就讓資料證明你的假設是錯的。

cues.en: And of course, you should always be curious in life, in general, and also when approaching data sets.
cues.zh: 當然，在生活中，以及面對資料集時，都應該保持好奇。

cues.en: You should always look at data, in particular, variability or differences in data and say, huh, why is that?
cues.zh: 看資料，尤其是資料的變異或差異時，應該問：「咦，為什麼？」

cues.en: Why are these differences there?
cues.zh: 為什麼有這些差異？

cues.en: What is causing these differences?
cues.zh: 是什麼造成這些差異？

cues.en: And then after you think that, your next thought should be, I wonder if I can actually test for that.
cues.zh: 思考之後，下一個念頭應該是：我是否真的能檢驗？

cues.en: Is this an hypothesis that I can test for in this data?
cues.zh: 這個假設能否用這些資料來檢驗？

cues.en: Or can I get some new data where I can actually test this hypothesis?
cues.zh: 或者，能否取得新資料，實際檢驗這個假設？

cues.en: Of course, that doesn't mean that you need to test every possible hypothesis, but it's good to be curious and open-minded.
cues.zh: 當然，這不表示每個可能的假設都必須檢驗，但保持好奇與開放很好。

cues.en: All right, so that is the end of this section.
cues.zh: 這一節就到這裡。

cues.en: Again, I hope you found it a useful, interesting and inspiring real world case study of importing a a real data set, processing the data,
cues.zh: 再次希望，這是個實用、有趣、能啟發你的真實案例，展示如何匯入真實資料集、處理資料，

cues.en: working through some problems and missing data, and trying to understand and statistically analyze the data.
cues.zh: 解決一些問題與遺失資料，並試著理解資料與進行統計分析。
